protocol.py: 6 biology problems (3 warnings, 3 notes).

1. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
   line 78:  p20.dispense(2.5, plate[sample_well_names[i]])
   At line 78 the robot put polymerase into wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more
   in slot 3 (this line did it 12 times). Take well A1 in slot 3: at that moment it held
   only 10 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 81, to make the
   20.5 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol
   and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have
   brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets
   many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star
   activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3:
   water and buffer first, then the sample, then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of
   water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [997f8e94d9e0]

2. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (tube A5 in slot 2)
   line 80:  p20.aspirate(10.5, tuberack["A5"])
   At line 80 the tip went into water (tube A5 in slot 2) while it still carried buffer
   (tube A1 in slot 2), polymerase (tube A2 in slot 2), fwd primer (tube A3 in slot 2) and
   rev primer (tube A4 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid
   leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material
   that does not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into
   wells that were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is
   left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tube A5 in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 80 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [5b9f7e9d888d]

   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling

5. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 12 wells of polymerase with a sample
   line 78:  p20.dispense(2.5, plate[sample_well_names[i]])
   At line 78 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 3), and 12 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 4 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 1.78571 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in
   place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [4b40c4bc5675]

6. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 12 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 8 more went in (8% of the well)
   line 84:  p20.dispense(2, plate[sample_well_names[i]])
   At line 84 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 8 more to wells A1,
   A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3, which already held buffer, polymerase,
   fwd primer, rev primer and 1 more (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 8% of the
   well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two
   liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before
   cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3 after line 84:
   `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide

findings.explanation: At line 78 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 3), and 12 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 1.78571 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 12 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 8 more went in (8% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 84 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 8 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3, which already held buffer, polymerase, fwd primer, rev primer and 1 more (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 8% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3 after line 84: `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
